(a) Reauthorization.—Section 738A(b) (21 U.S.C. 379j–1(b)) is amended—
        (1) in paragraph (1), by striking “2012” and inserting “2017”; and 
        (2) in paragraph (5), by striking “2012” and inserting “2017”.  
    (b) Performance Reports.—Section 738A(a) (21 U.S.C. 379j–1(a)) is amended—
        (1) by striking paragraph (1) and inserting the following:“(1) Performance report.—“(A) In general.—Beginning with fiscal year 2013, for each fiscal year for which fees are collected under this part, the Secretary shall prepare and submit to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions of the Senate and the Committee on Energy and Commerce of the House of Representatives annual reports concerning the progress of the Food and Drug Administration in achieving the goals identified in the letters described in section 201(b) of the Medical Device User Fee Amendments of 2012 during such fiscal year and the future plans of the Food and Drug Administration for meeting the goals.“(B) Publication.—With regard to information to be reported by the Food and Drug Administration to industry on a quarterly and annual basis pursuant to the letters described in section 201(b) of the Medical Device User Fee Amendments Act of 2012, the Secretary shall make such information publicly available on the Internet Web site of the Food and Drug Administration not later than 60 days after the end of each quarter or 120 days after the end of each fiscal year, respectively, to which such information applies. This information shall include the status of the independent assessment identified in the letters described in such section 201(b).“(C) Updates.—The Secretary shall include in each report under subparagraph (A) information on all previous cohorts for which the Secretary has not given a complete response on all device premarket applications and reports, 
supplements, and premarket notifications in the cohort.”; and 
        (2) in paragraph (2), by striking “2008 through 2012” and inserting “2013 through 2017”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that performance reporting, publishing information reported "to industry", and reauthorizing section 738A(b) amount to participation. But the reports go to congressional committees, which are inside the federal government, and posting information on the FDA website is one-way disclosure, not consultation before a decision. The reauthorization amendments only change dates ("2012" to "2017"); the underlying section 738A(b) may contain consultation requirements, but nothing in this section's own text establishes an outside-party process.
fable.s: the Secretary shall prepare and submit to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions of the Senate and the Committee on Energy and Commerce of the House of Representatives annual reports

opus.w: The main requirement is an annual report to congressional committees, which stays inside the federal government. Posting information on the FDA website and reporting to industry are one-way disclosures, not consultation with outsiders before a federal decision. The amendments to § 738A(b) only change dates. They don't put any outside-party consultation, hearing, or comment period into the text shown, though the underlying provision might contain stakeholder consultation, which lowers confidence somewhat.
opus.s: the Secretary shall prepare and submit to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions of the Senate and the Committee on Energy and Commerce of the House of Representatives annual reports concerning the progress of the Food and Drug Administration
opus.b:
1. **The tempting reading.** The section mentions information "reported by the Food and Drug Administration to industry" and requires posting information "publicly available on the Internet Web site." It also amends § 738A(b), which in the underlying law sets up stakeholder consultation and public meetings for reauthorization. Any of these could look like participation by outsiders.

2. **Why it doesn't hold.** The annual reports go to two congressional committees, and Congress is inside the federal government. Posting information online and reporting to industry are one-way disclosures. No outside party is consulted before a federal decision. The § 738A(b) changes only swap "2012" for "2017." No consultation, hearing, comment period, or advisory body appears in the text shown.

qwen_chat.w: The section requires the Secretary to submit reports to Congressional committees, which are part of the federal government (inside). While it also requires making some information publicly available on the FDA website, this is a transparency measure rather than a process of consultation, coordination, or advisory input from outside parties before a decision is made. Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: the Secretary shall prepare and submit to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions of the Senate and the Committee on Energy and Commerce of the House of Representatives annual reports
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that making information "publicly available on the Internet Web site" constitutes participation because it involves the general public. However, the definition specifies that participation involves consulting or coordinating with outsiders *before* making a decision, or granting rights to sue/object. Mere publication of reports or data for transparency is not interactive participation in the decision-making process. Furthermore, the primary reporting requirement is to Congressional committees, which are inside the federal government.
